attribution.osm: Centerline and width measurement derived from OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
attribution.sentinel: Chips and corridor metrics contain modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026).

claims.text: Fly-ash dredging of the creek complex is an active WRD programme (~4.30 lakh m3 scope since 2020).
No canal-specific outfall is documented on this reach; the load arrives with the creek system.
TNPCB's fish-kill investigation (Aug 2026) is live; Kamarajar Port and TANGEDCO interfaces govern access.
NCSCM's Rs 45.99 crore creek eco-restoration (2023-25) is in progress under NGT OA 152/2023.

Fly-ash silting about 1 m deep on the 2.5 km NCTPS-Kamarajar stretch; WRD dredging of ~4.30 lakh cubic metres began mid-2020 under NGT direction, funded by a Rs 28.5 crore Tangedco deposit plus Rs 66.23 lakh for the North Buckingham Canal.
claims.source: The Hindu via ICSF; NGT record

claims.text: A mass fish kill hit this reach 15-17 Aug 2026 (~6-7 km, Kattukuppam to Kolivakkam): tonnes of mullet, ladyfish, croakers, prawns and crabs. Fishers blocked the Ennore expressway. TNPCB lab results pending.
claims.source: The South First; The Federal; Deccan Chronicle

claims.text: A citizen field study measured water at 40.8 C in the canal near the Railway Bridge, 585 m from NTECL Vallur's discharge point, on 9 Aug 2026, and attributes the kill to hot-water and chemical discharge. This attribution is the campaign's, not TNPCB's.
claims.source: Save Ennore Creek Campaign press release

claims.text: The invasive charru mussel (Mytella strigata) has colonised the Kosasthalaiyar backwater and the canal; NCSCM found it at ~24% of 197 sampling points at densities above 800 per sq m. WRD sought Rs 160 crore from Kamarajar Port for removal.
Ash slurry pipeline crossings and reported dead-flow spots define the channel condition here.
claims.source: The News Minute; India Water Portal

claims.text: Power-station cooling circuits (consented into the creek) shape the hydraulics.
Ash slurry pipelines cross the canal en route to the NCTPS ash pond; reporting found spots where canal flow is completely dead nearest the plant, with low tide exposing thick ash-silt deposits.
claims.source: The News Minute; India Water Portal

claims.text: On current consents, NCTPS Stages I and II are permitted to discharge 2.38 and 4.90 million KLD of once-through cooling water respectively 'into Ennore Creek' - the largest consented discharges in the creek system.
CPCL's consented monsoon stormwater route enters here, with online sensors and booms as consent conditions.
Refinery-belt access and the Dec 2023 oil-spill legacy govern works planning.

On TNPCB's current consent books, no Manali process industry may discharge effluent to the canal: CPCL is reuse-only (with a consented monsoon stormwater route to the canal, monitored by online sensors and booms), Indian Additives and Ashok Leyland are zero-liquid-discharge, TPL discharges to sea.
claims.source: 13 TNPCB OCMMS consent orders, pulled 18 Aug 2026

claims.text: TNPCB's Manali CEPI action plan states there is 'no disposal of treated trade effluent/sewage into Buckingham canal', attributing the canal's load to 7.8 MLD of untreated municipal sewage from local bodies without underground sewerage.
claims.source: TNPCB CEPI action plan for Manali

claims.text: During Cyclone Michaung flooding on 4 Dec 2023, an estimated 24,000 litres of CPCL crude entered the Buckingham Canal and spread through it to the creek and sea, affecting ~20 sq km and ~9 fishing villages; 2,301 fisher families were compensated Rs 8.68 crore.
Ashok Leyland's Ennore consent expired on 31 Mar 2026 with no renewal visible in the public OCMMS search as of 18 Aug 2026; it may sit in TNPCB's non-public auto-renewal scheme.
Three Kodungaiyur STP outlets (40+80+110 MLD) and six Tiruvottiyur pumping stations (>=7.25 MLD raw) are the documented inflows - the densest interception workload on the canal.
claims.source: TNPCB CCWW 2022-23; Arappor Iyakkam RTI audit

claims.text: Kodungaiyur dumpyard bank; the city's worst Culex clusters flank this reach.
The Kodungaiyur STP cluster's 40, 80 and 110 MLD outlets discharge to this reach; TNPCB files them under 'Buckingham Canal River'. In 2022-23 the 80 MLD outlet hit BOD 51 mg/L against a 10 mg/L norm.
Six CMWSSB pumping stations in Tiruvottiyur discharge at least 7.25 MLD of raw sewage directly into the canal, per CMWSSB's own RTI replies reproduced in a citizens' audit.
Median measured water width on this reach: 25 m.
Tondiarpet, Old Washermanpet, Korukkupet and Mint, alongside the canal, are the city's worst Culex mosquito clusters; the canal is GCC's named top breeding source.
claims.source: Madras Musings; Citizen Matters (GCC vector control)

claims.text: Otteri Nullah and the Captain Cotton Canal join at Basin Bridge - two of the city's largest drain loads arrive here.
Otteri Nullah (38.4 sq km catchment) and the Captain Cotton Canal join the Buckingham Canal at Basin Bridge.
claims.source: IIT Madras rapid assessment of the 2015 flood

claims.text: CPCB's Captain Cotton Canal station recorded dissolved oxygen as low as 0.3 mg/L and BOD up to 120 mg/L in 2024.
The city squeeze begins: rail infrastructure hems the channel past Central and the yards.
Rail-yard land interfaces (Southern Railway) govern any widening here.
The North Canal joins the Cooum's north bank at grade behind Chennai Central; there is no continuous canal channel through the junction.
This is the tidal Cooum itself: works here belong to the Cooum restoration scope, not canal packages.
TNPCB's Feb 2025 sampling found the canal's salinity maxima near Napier Bridge (TDS 5,560 mg/L, chloride 2,599 mg/L): the tidal signature of the Cooum mouth.

The South Buckingham Canal is a tidal canal taking off from the Cooum and running 110 km to Kovalam North lock near Marakkanam, with seven sea openings, lock-controlled, whose sand bars keep them closed about seven months a year.
Bridge vents at Ice House Road and Kutchery Road were built 5-6 m against a required 15-17 m and were never widened (CAG); vent widening is a named, unfinished work item.
Width recovery envelope: recorded 42-143 m on this link, measured median 18 m today (the width ledger carries the road-by-road detail).
The sewage mitigation plan ordered by the High Court (2022) applies with full force here - the Wallajah Road monitoring station records the load.
MRTS pillars are exempt from the HC removal order; demarcation stalled in the central constituencies.
Measured water width on this reach: median 18 m, minimum 9.3 m.
IWAI's condition survey found the city stretch 'totally in abandoned condition', width 10-15 m, with MRTS columns standing in the canal bed itself.
Original survey widths between the Cooum and Adyar ran 42 m (Wallajah Road) to 143 m (St Mary's Road); current widths 24-48 m.
claims.source: HSCTC feasibility report (~2012), via Wikipedia (table added 25 Aug 2013)

claims.text: CPCB's Ice House station recorded DO pinned at 0.3 mg/L through all of 2024, with BOD up to 141 mg/L - the worst year in the five-edition record.
TNPCB's Wallajah Road station logged monthly BOD between 9 (December, monsoon flush) and 150 mg/L (April) in 2022-23. The monitoring series ends there: no CCWW edition has been published since.
claims.source: TNPCB CCWW 2022-23; TNPCB waterquality page checked 18 Aug 2026

claims.text: The Central-canal flood-wall programme collapsed from 14,200 m to 1,115 m over eviction constraints (Rs 68.62 cr sanction, Rs 15.72 cr spent) - the remaining wall length is a known, unfinished quantity.
Unauthorised sewer connections from bank settlements are the documented local load.
About 5,000 houses stand on the banks; the 2023 DPR for these reaches was set aside in Nov 2024 pending funds, with a successor proposal filed Oct 2025.
The MRTS was routed on the canal per a 1976-77 Planning Commission working group because no other corridor was economically available; the 2022 High Court order exempts its pillars from removal.

Around Mylapore roughly 5,000 houses stand on the canal banks; the 2023 restoration DPR for these reaches was set aside in Nov 2024 pending funds, and a fresh Rs 2,388 crore proposal to the Centre followed in Oct 2025.
claims.source: Citizen Matters / The News Minute; Hindusthan Samachar

claims.text: CAG found 17% of the canal's banks (16.5 of 96 km) encroached by 26,300 families, extended electricity, roads, water and ration cards.
claims.source: CAG Report No. 4 of 2017, Chapter IV

claims.text: Two decades of canal- and river-bank evictions moved ~19,817 families (~79,000 people, 2015-2023) largely to Kannagi Nagar, Ezhil Nagar and Perumbakkam - resettlement colonies built on the very marshland-floodplain this canal drains, which themselves flood.
claims.source: IRCDUC, 'Resettled in the Paths of Floods'

claims.text: The Adyar estuary junction: works here interact with Adyar-mouth dredging and the eco-park reach.
The 2015 Adyar peak entering the city was ~3,800 cubic metres per second against a channel capacity of ~2,038.
Govindasamy Nagar, on PWD canal land here, was demolished from Apr 2022 after a 2011 Supreme Court ruling; families were dispersed to four resettlement sites.
Eight MRTS crossings define the constriction pattern; hyacinth-removal machinery has worked this reach (2021 CM inspection).

In Sep 2021 the Chief Minister inspected pre-monsoon hyacinth removal with floating amphibian machines and robotic excavators on the canal near Indira Nagar MRTS station and Thiruvanmiyur Lattice Bridge.
CMRL's vent-way programme at the Okkiyam crossing (widened to 200 m, clearance raised, bed desilted toward a 12,000-cusec capacity) is the active works precedent on the canal.
Perungudi-side STP discharges (54+60 MLD plus Alandur and Sholinganallur) arrive via the Pallikaranai system.
Okkiyam Maduvu falls inside the Pallikaranai Ramsar boundary; CMDA froze planning permissions in the 1 km zone (Office Order 07/2025). Evidence-first is the only lawful entry.
Okkiyam Maduvu, a 2.8 km channel, is the sole outlet of the ~250 sq km Pallikaranai drainage (65 wetlands) into the canal, and the marsh's only brackish link to the sea at Muttukadu.
claims.source: TN State Wetlands Authority; Suzhal Arivom

claims.text: Metro Phase 2 viaduct works narrowed the channel under the OMR bridge from a pre-construction 83.73 m to under 10 m (field observations from 6 May 2026); a second constriction sat at the Perumbakkam outlet; both sites fall inside the notified Ramsar boundary, within the crossing CMRL's vent-way widening programme serves.

Zero flamingo records anywhere in Pallikaranai from 1 Jan to 15 Jun 2026, attributed by the field report to the blocked tidal exchange; water hyacinth proliferated across both sides of the obstruction.

Our satellite screening independently shows this reach's corridor vegetation fraction jumping from 0.58 (Jan-Apr 2026) to 0.77 (Jun-Aug 2026), consistent with the documented hyacinth explosion; monsoon bank-greening also contributes, so ground-truth decides.
Modelling of the 2015 flood simulated a peak of 1,349.5 cubic metres per second (~47,700 cusecs) through Okkiyam Maduvu; the channel's stated capacity after post-Michaung works is 12,000 cusecs.

In 2015, absence of the dropped short-cut diversion channel forced 12,500 cusecs into a canal reach designed for 9,000, inundating Velachery and adjacent areas. The channel had been dropped in Oct 2014 after Rs 90.34 crore of a Rs 131.90 crore sanction was spent, over land acquisition costed at about Rs 100 crore.
CAG records the 9,000-cusec improvement completed Dec 2014; a 2025 field check saw ~2.5 km visibly widened - an as-built verification survey would reconcile the records.
Sholinganallur STP (18 MLD) discharges on this system.
The 20 ha mangrove plantation (>90% survival) is a live restoration asset any works must design around - and can extend (fishbone technique, ~200 ha potential).

The Forest Department's Green Tamil Nadu Mission planted 12,500 mangrove saplings across ~20 ha on the Muttukadu-Pallikaranai stretch in 2024 using a fishbone channel technique, with over 90% survival; 20,000 more seedlings followed in 2025-26.

CAG records the JNNURM improvement of this reach (to carry 9,000 cusecs) as completed in December 2014; a 2025 field check reported only ~2.5 km visibly widened to Injambakkam bridge; a field verification would reconcile the two records.
claims.source: CAG Report No. 4 of 2017 vs Uvakai Research Foundation field check

claims.text: Cement residue and construction debris were documented being dumped on the canal's outer embankments between Akkarai signal and Sholinganallur in June 2024, threatening South Chennai's primary flood outlet.
Median measured water width on this reach: 42 m - against 18 m in the MRTS reaches.
The Rs 91 cr Uthandi straight-cut (550 cusecs) is under construction from this reach to the sea; the abandoned Muttukadu Boat House Lock anchors the south end.
CRZ objections and fisher protests accompanied the straight-cut's start - stakeholder interface is live.

The Uthandi straight-cut flood escape channel (Rs 91 crore, 550 cusecs capacity against the canal's 3,500) was tendered 8 Jul 2025 and started amid CRZ objections and fisher protests; water tests en route found faecal coliform 1,600 MPN/100ml and BOD 26.5 mg/L.
The Muthukadu Boat House Lock, one of three abandoned navigation locks on the southern canal, stands at 12.8073 N 80.2414 E.
Mouth management is budgeted (MAWS Rs 1 cr to dredge and hold a 100 m opening); IWAI's 2014 scheme priced lock rebuilds at Muttukadu and Kovalam South.
NGT filings admit sewage discharges reaching the estuary; tanker dumping was caught here.
claims.source: CMWSSB report to NGT; Citizen Matters

claims.text: Olive ridley nesting beaches adjoin the mouth (Jan-Apr season); TTDC tourism and CIBA's research station operate on the backwater.

Muttukadu is a temporarily open/closed estuary: longshore drift closes the mouth roughly March-September; the monsoon reopens it; the mouth varies from a few metres to ~200 m. Water quality deteriorates sharply when closed, with recorded hypoxia fish kills.
126 bird species are on the live eBird list for Muttukadu Backwaters (captured 18 Aug 2026), corroborating the 2024 journal survey's 124 species (Jul 2021-Mar 2023 fieldwork, 7 near-threatened).
The brackish reaches read nearly vegetation-free in our satellite screening (0.09-0.12) while freshwater stagnant reaches choke - the salinity control on hyacinth, visible from orbit.
MAWS agreed Rs 1 crore to dredge and hold a 100 m opening at the mouth; TTDC (whose 1984 boat house anchors backwater tourism) sought WRD dredging.
Olive ridley nesting beaches run from the Adyar mouth south past Kovalam (Jan-Apr season); any works at this mouth sit beside an active nesting beach.
Kovalam creek mangrove restoration has a identified phase-2 site (100 acres near Kelambakkam toll).
The proposed Mamallan reservoir would convert the adjoining Kovalam-Nemmeli wetland; 22 scientists have written to the CM - scope interacts with a live policy question.

The Kovalam-Nemmeli 'Great Salt Lake' (~5,000 acres) is a hand-fishery and shorebird wetland fed twice daily by tides through the Muttukadu and Kokilamedu inlets; the canal carries catchment surplus through it.

The proposed Mamallan reservoir would convert the wetland for 170 MLD of city supply; the project EIA itself recorded 102 bird species, and 22 scientists wrote to the Chief Minister warning of irreversible damage.

7,000 Avicennia marina saplings were planted in Kovalam creek in 2022-23 after clearing invasive Prosopis, with Irula community help; 100 acres near the Kelambakkam toll plaza are identified for phase 2.
Eleven structure-free kilometres with intact banks: the largest uninterrupted works canvas on the alignment; the channel currently runs vegetation-choked.
Our satellite screening shows this reach as a continuous vegetated channel with almost no open water at 10 m resolution (corridor vegetation 0.55-0.61, water near zero) - see the km 64-66 chip.
IWAI's survey found the southern canal's banks unprotected up to the Mahabalipuram Road Bridge, with depths of 0.3-1.3 m.
IWAI's 2014 scheme placed a terminal here (never built); the canal continues south toward Kalpakkam.
The Mamallapuram monuments zone (~1.5 km east) brings heritage-authority interfaces.
IWAI's 2014 scheme placed a proposed Mahabalipuram terminal at 12.6169 N 80.1868 E; the Rs 123.40 crore Thiruvanmiyur-Kalpakkam development stalled with ~Rs 4 crore spent.
South of scope, the canal continues toward Kalpakkam, where the MAPS cooling-water return raises canal level up to 20 cm for 20 km.

Built 1806-1882 to carry salt, firewood and dried fish into Madras, the Buckingham Canal today is Chennai's flood carrier and the spine of the city's eastern waterways: 74.5 km, measured here end to end, two hundred metres at a time.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Regulation has steadily moved industry's routine discharges off the canal; what remains to manage is the city's sewage and the storm-season event. Continuous measurement is how the next question gets answered in hours.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Between the Cooum and the Adyar, survey records give the canal 42 to 143 metres; today's water measures 9 at the narrowest. Restoration mathematics starts from the measured number, and this page carries it every 200 metres.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Everything South Chennai drains passes through one 2.8 km channel into the canal. It is the system's most sensitive point: weather, works and weeds all register here first, which is why it rewards the closest watch.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Where the tide still reaches, the canal still lives: 126 bird species, working fishers, a boat house - behind a sand bar that closes seven months a year.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: South of Kovalam the canal is intact and quiet: eleven structure-free kilometres, banks unbroken, running green with vegetation - the alignment's readiest restoration canvas.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Since 2008 the canal has gathered a national-waterway designation, a High Court restoration mandate, audits and sanctions - and in 2026, the largest funding window in its history. The intent is aligned; this page is the baseline to build on.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Rs 7,500 crore of restoration intent now converges on these waterways. Investment at that scale deserves a live measurement layer: this page is the baseline, and a pilot is what keeps it current.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Canal declared part of National Waterway 4
JNNURM macro-drainage sanction incl. canal widening and a short-cut diversion channel
Diversion channel discontinued after Rs 90.34 cr of works; IWAI's Rs 123.40 cr Thiruvanmiyur-Kalpakkam scheme launched (~Rs 4 cr of works recorded)
The December flood: 12,500 cusecs forced into a 9,000-cusec reach; Velachery inundated
CAG quantifies 242.73 MLD of raw sewage entering CMA water bodies incl. the canal (CMWSSB estimate, Apr 2019)
KfW Kovalam-basin and ADB Kosasthalaiyar-basin drainage programmes (outfalls to the canal system)
Madras HC orders demarcation in 6 months, encroachment removal in 1 year, IWAI custody; MRTS pillars exempted; sewage mitigation plan ordered
WRD restoration DPR submitted (Anna University DGPS survey)
Umbrella sanction for canal + associated drains + Adyar/Cooum major drains (G.O. unidentified; boundary-stone stage)
Uthandi straight-cut tendered (550 cusecs); PWD proposes full-canal restoration to the Centre; Rs 31 cr Chepauk-Greenways starter with IWAI; water-metro feasibility begins
Centre approves Urban Challenge Fund phase 1 for Cooum-Adyar-Buckingham restoration; CMRL floats the Water Metro DFR-cum-DPR tender for Ennore-Mahabalipuram (bids close 18 Sep 2026)
claims.source: Swarajya 11 Jun 2026; CMRL NIT TDR-76-WM/2026 dt 13 Aug 2026

The last published depth survey of the southern canal found 0.3 to 1.3 m of water against a 1.8 m navigation target; no public bathymetry has been recorded since. A boat-run depth transect is the pilot's first field deliverable.
At the Ennore end, fly-ash silt about 1 m deep on a 2.5 km stretch is under a WRD dredging programme (~4.30 lakh cubic metres) running since mid-2020.
claims.source: The Hindu via ICSF; NGT record

claims.text: Ahead of Cyclone Michaung, reporting put the bed at 2 ft below mean sea level against a historical 6 ft - the working measure of accumulated silt in the city reaches.
GCC removed 16,270 tonnes of silt and water hyacinth from 44 canals and water bodies between 2 May and 10 July 2026 in monsoon preparation; per-canal splits are with the contracts.
The Oct 2025 restoration proposal prices dredging the full 167 km to a uniform 1.5-3.0 m depth - the clearest official statement of where depths stand today.
132 ha - vegetation on the corridor this window (weed mats, reeds and bank growth together)
~58 ha - open water visible from orbit, concentrated at the Ennore, Muttukadu and Kelambakkam reaches
7 of 18 - reaches with enough open water for a suspended-sediment reading; the Adyar crossing reads highest

2,239 vs 0 - buildings within 50 m of the centerline: the Okkiyam belt reach vs the southern ribbon. The zero is verified against the unfiltered dataset; the nearest village sits beyond 200 m of the alignment
claims.source: Google Open Buildings v3 (2023 release, confidence >= 0.7); Neer Vazhvu proximity analysis
